steps.body: Stories name the whole and the pieces in words: read for how many EQUAL pieces the whole became, then how many the story is about.
steps.narration: Stories name the whole and the pieces in words: read for how many EQUAL pieces the whole became, then how many the story is about.

widget.prompt: A ribbon is cut into 6 equal pieces and 5 are used. Build the fraction used.
widget.successFeedback: 5/6 — six equal pieces made, five of them used.
widget.lowFeedback: Your shaded amount is less than the target 5/6. Compare it with the target, then increase the shaded amount.
widget.highFeedback: Your shaded amount is greater than the target 5/6. Compare it with the target, then decrease the shaded amount.

commonFractions.feedback: That flipped the numbers: sixths are the piece size, so 6 belongs underneath.
1/6 names a single piece, but five pieces were used.

predict.prompt: A ribbon in 6 equal pieces, 5 used. Which number goes on the bottom?
predict.reveal: The bottom always names how many equal pieces the whole became; the top counts the ones in question.

cml.actionGoal: Cut, count, and compare equal pieces to see what g3f story really names.
invariants: A fraction names equal shares of ONE whole: the denominator says how many equal pieces the whole became, and the numerator counts them, which is what makes g3f story comparable at all.
misconceptions: Calling unequal pieces fractions, reading the denominator as a count, or comparing fractions that came from different-sized wholes.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the whole changed size, which of these comparisons would stop being trustworthy?

widget.prompt: A carton holds 10 eggs and 7 are used for baking. Which fraction names what was used?

options.label: 7/10 — seven of ten eggs
options.feedback: Correct — the denominator counts the equal parts the carton holds, and the numerator counts the ones used.

options.label: 10/7 — ten eggs, seven used
options.feedback: That puts the whole on top; the carton's count belongs underneath, and 10/7 would be more than one carton.

options.label: 3/10 — the eggs left over
options.feedback: 3/10 names what REMAINS in the carton, but the question asks for the part that was used.

options.label: 1/10 — one egg was used
options.feedback: 1/10 names a single egg, but seven of them were used, not one.

widget.prompt: A baker uses 3/8 of a bag of flour for bread and 4/8 of the bag for buns. Express the total used as ?/8. What is the numerator?

commonErrors.feedback: 8 names the piece size; adding same-size pieces changes only how MANY you have.
Multiplying the counts is not joining them — 3 pieces and 4 more pieces make 7.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Name the equal pieces the whole was cut into, then count how many of them the question is about.

options.label: 6/5 — six pieces, five used

options.label: 1/6 — one piece was used
options.feedback: 1/6 names a single piece, but five of them were used, not one.

options.label: 1/5 — five pieces

widget.prompt: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices and 3 are eaten. Which fraction names what was eaten?

options.feedback: Correct — the denominator counts the equal slices the whole became, and the numerator counts the ones eaten.

options.label: 8/3 — eight slices, three eaten
options.feedback: That puts the whole on top; the slice count belongs underneath, and 8/3 would be more than one pizza.

options.label: 1/8 — one slice was eaten
options.feedback: 1/8 names a single slice, but three of them were eaten, not one.

options.label: 1/3 — three slices
options.feedback: The pizza was cut into EIGHT slices, so eighths are the piece size no matter how many were eaten.
